title: Exact use-only cross-project grants and revocation
description: Spec §7.2. One owner secret, one target project, one target alias; use only; no wildcard; revocation blocks new admissions.

acceptanceCriteria.text: ward secret grant <alias> --to <project-id> --as <alias> and ward secret revoke <alias> --from <project-id> are in ward manifest --json and ward help; a grant creates the sharingGrants record (owner project, owner secret id, target project, target alias); target list shows the alias marked granted and inspect reports ownership; no value, length, preview or hash appears

In a registered target checkout an approved profile naming the granted alias runs; the owner current value reaches only the approved auth header; a test updates the owner value and proves the next target run uses it (T12)
The target cannot update, delete or re-grant the owner record: each attempt exits 4 with a fixed catalogue code, writes no vault revision and leaves the owner record byte-identical (T12)

Revocation and owner deletion block new admissions: ward run then exits with a fixed code, makes no network attempt and writes no admission or completion audit record; an operation admitted before revocation may finish and the report states the admission-time rule (T12, ADR 0003)

Restore clears grants and approvals (Q2): a test restores a vault that held a grant and proves the target cannot run without fresh approval and re-grant, with a positive control that the same profile runs before the restore (T21)
docs/security-tests.md gains T12 and T21 rows naming the test and recorded result; bun run check and the three required CI contexts pass on the merge SHA

implementationNotes: Design per DEC-217 Q1/Q2, recorded as ADR 0020. Choices put to review: (1) grant is interactive (terminal approver, unavailable is never consent), revoke is not; DEC-217 is silent. (2) completion no longer re-resolves the alias: an admitted run finishes and records against the admission secret id, where before a mid-flight owner delete turned a sent request into auditRecorded=false. (3) revoked grants stay as tombstones; owner delete revokes its grants in the same write; the reader and serializer both refuse active-grant relations that do not hold. (4) secret list gained an ownership field and granted entries carry null updatedAt/revision. Local lore is 0.14.1 against the 0.13.0 CI pin, so lore check shows 11 schema-drift errors that are the local binary, not this change; lore validate --strict is clean.
